entities.name: PMID:10731001
observations: Rat study after 8 weeks of fish oil or soy oil with or without vitamin E, including exhaustive acute-exercise subgroups.
Vitamin E counter-regulated fish-oil-associated antioxidant-enzyme changes and increased total glutathione in liver, heart, and red gastrocnemius.
Vitamin E reduced fish-oil-associated oxidative damage; effects on acute-exercise oxidative damage were less consistent.

entities.name: PMID:9216963
observations: Rat study after 8 weeks of fish oil or soy oil with or without vitamin E, assessing oxidative stress at rest and after exhaustive exercise.

Fish oil increased hepatic TBARS; vitamin E reduced lipid peroxidation and protein carbonyls, while several exercise-related oxidative-damage outcomes were similar between vitamin-E and control exercise groups.

entities.name: Vitamin E
observations: In PMID:10731001, vitamin E decreased fish-oil-associated catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and glutathione-S-transferase activities toward soy-oil plus vitamin-E levels, in a tissue-specific manner.
Vitamin E increased or preserved total glutathione and reduced oxidative damage measures.

entities.name: Fish oil
observations: In PMID:10731001, fish oil increased catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and glutathione-S-transferase activities and decreased hepatic total glutathione.
Fish oil increased oxidative stress-related measures in the companion study PMID:9216963.

entities.name: Vitamin E counter-regulation
observations: In rats receiving fish oil for 8 weeks, vitamin E counter-regulated fish-oil-associated tissue antioxidant-enzyme changes and increased total glutathione.
The acute-exercise interaction was not uniform across oxidative-damage endpoints.
